registered_moa: heat-shock response co-inducer (no mechanism row in Open Targets)
hypothesised_mechanism: chaperone co-induction raising the fraction of destabilised p.Asn1002Lys that survives quality control
mechanism_is_registered: the mechanism IS the lever; indication is a different disease
mechanism_basis_note: heat-shock response co-induction is arimoclomol's defining and well-documented pharmacology; it is simply not carried as a mechanism row, and the registered indication is another disease
approval_source: openFDA /drug/ndc (product level) + Open Targets maximumClinicalStage (substance level)
product_level_verified: YES - FDA NDA (MIPLYFFA, capsule, marketing start 2024-09-20); approved in COMBINATION with miglustat for neurological manifestations of Niemann-Pick disease type C in adult and paediatric patients 2 years and older
key_counter_evidence: Approved only in COMBINATION with miglustat, so standalone use in another disease is off-label monotherapy - every candidate here is off-label, but this one also departs from its label's regimen. Enhancing proteostasis is an antidote to aneuploidy-selective vulnerability, so it may protect pre-malignant aneuploid cells in a child who already has a sarcoma. Open Targets 26.09 still records PHASE_3 and carries no mechanism row; the approval was confirmed against openFDA, which returns the MIPLYFFA NDA directly.
verdict: mechanistically the closest available lever, and the only candidate with product-level approval confirmed

registered_moa: SEQUESTERING AGENT: glutamine sequestering agent (ChEMBL CHEMBL1746) - nitrogen scavenging for urea-cycle disorders, NOT the chaperone activity proposed here
hypothesised_mechanism: chemical chaperone raising the fraction of p.Asn1002Lys that survives quality control
mechanism_is_registered: no - registered mechanism is nitrogen scavenging, not chaperoning
mechanism_basis_note: chemical-chaperone activity is established pharmacology (CFTR trafficking, ER-stress reduction); the registered mechanism is nitrogen scavenging
approval_source: openFDA /drug/ndc (product level) + Open Targets maximumClinicalStage (substance level)
key_counter_evidence: TWO documented activities pull in OPPOSITE directions on this target. As a chemical chaperone it should raise the fraction of destabilised p.Asn1002Lys surviving quality control - the lever we want. But it is also a non-competitive HDAC inhibitor, and an HDAC-inhibition signature is exactly what we observed in GSE86928 (HIST1H1C +2.08 with MKI67 -3.7, CCNA2 -4.6, FOXM1 -3.0) alongside BUB1B falling 2.4-fold, while our signed network requires BUB1B to rise. The drug's own second pharmacology therefore EXPLAINS our counter-evidence rather than merely coinciding with it: a proteostatic gain would have to overcome a transcriptional loss the same molecule causes. Neither activity is its registered mechanism (ChEMBL records only glutamine sequestering). Limits on the counter-evidence stand: n=1 per condition, 5 mM is supra-therapeutic, A549 is a cancer line, and expression is the wrong assay for a post-translational hypothesis - the protein-level measurement is what settles it.
verdict: highest ceiling in the project, lowest probability

hypothesised_mechanism: muscle-directed therapy registered for a different muscular disorder
mechanism_basis_note: HDAC inhibition is the registered mechanism; what differs is the disease, not the mechanism
approval_source: openFDA /drug/ndc (product level) + Open Targets maximumClinicalStage (substance level)
key_counter_evidence: Duchenne muscular dystrophy is a listed indication, so the match is indication-level in another disease. Ceiling is 2 because muscle function is a major clinical burden rather than one lab value. Direct tension with this project's own expression evidence: an HDAC-inhibitor signature is exactly what drives the checkpoint transcripts down in GSE86928. Note the internal tension across arms: givinostat is an HDAC inhibitor, and HDAC inhibition is the activity arguing AGAINST the causal-arm phenylbutyrate candidate. The same class is being proposed for muscle and counted against BUBR1 dose, which is defensible only because the arms answer different questions - but it must be visible rather than left for a reader to notice.
verdict: real ceiling, with a mechanism conflict against our own data

registered_moa: no mechanism row in Open Targets, and none in ChEMBL either
hypothesised_mechanism: urinary alkalinisation and citrate repletion - mechanism asserted from literature, not from a registered row
mechanism_basis_note: urinary alkalinisation and citrate repletion is the action behind its approved renal indications
approval_source: openFDA /drug/ndc (product level) + Open Targets maximumClinicalStage (substance level)
product_level_verified: YES - FDA 2 NDA + 12 ANDA (also an OTC monograph form)
key_counter_evidence: Downgraded from the previous pass on two checks. (1) Nephrocalcinosis is NOT among its 11 registered indications - those are Calcium nephrolithiasis, Uric acid nephrolithiasis, nephrolithiasis, renal tubular acidosis, CKD and metabolic acidosis. Stones and parenchymal calcium deposition are different conditions, so the grade is 2, not 3. (2) The previous pass recorded 'urinary alkalinisation' as the registered mechanism; Open Targets records NO mechanism row, so that was supplied from knowledge - a breach of this project's own first rule. Risk raised to 1 for potassium loading where renal function may be impaired. Ceiling is low: partial relief of one feature that may be secondary to prematurity and resolves spontaneously in most preterm infants.
verdict: mild, supplement-grade benefit at best - which is now what the score says

hypothesised_mechanism: reduces urinary calcium excretion, the mechanism driving calcium deposition
mechanism_basis_note: the hypocalciuric effect follows directly from the registered NCC-inhibition mechanism
approval_source: openFDA /drug/ndc (product level) + Open Targets maximumClinicalStage (substance level)
key_counter_evidence: CORRECTION to the previous pass, which stated the hypocalciuric indication was not registered. The Open Targets record lists Hypercalciuria, idiopathic hypercalciuria AND nephrolithiasis among 42 indications - so this is an indication-level match on the mechanism that drives the child's renal feature, not a mechanism-only match. Nephrocalcinosis itself is still not a listed indication, which is why the grade is 2 and not 3.
verdict: best-evidenced and most executable intervention for the renal feature

mechanism_basis_note: lysosomotropic blockade of autophagic flux is established pharmacology; the registered mechanism is TLR7/TLR9 antagonism

key_counter_evidence: Ceiling is 2 because tumour control is a major burden. Depends on a tumour-versus-tissue selective window that has NOT been demonstrated; if no window exists the correct verdict is a veto in both contexts.

hypothesised_mechanism: readthrough of the premature TGA created by c.2210T>G
mechanism_basis_note: readthrough of a premature stop IS the registered mechanism; what differs is the gene
approval_source: openFDA /drug/ndc (product level) + Open Targets maximumClinicalStage (substance level)
product_level_verified: NO - openFDA returns ONE record and it is BULK INGREDIENT only: no NDA, no ANDA, so there is no approved product in the United States. The EU conditional authorisation was reportedly not renewed in March 2025. Pending an EMA check this candidate may fail the project's own rule that only medicines already in human use qualify.
contraindication_flag: APPROVAL IN QUESTION - no US product; EU authorisation reportedly not renewed
key_counter_evidence: Ceiling is high but executability is the lowest here. Stop is TGA, the most permissive codon, but the +4 base read from the reference is A, the LEAST permissive position in the C>U>G>A hierarchy. Near-cognate decoding inserts Trp, Arg or Cys, not Leu. Transcript is NMD-competent and no NMD inhibitor is approved.

mechanism_is_registered: yes - nephrolithiasis is a listed indication
mechanism_basis_note: same registered NCC mechanism as hydrochlorothiazide
approval_source: openFDA /drug/ndc (product level) + Open Targets maximumClinicalStage (substance level)
key_counter_evidence: Nephrolithiasis is listed among 17 indications, but hypercalciuria is not - which is why it ranks below hydrochlorothiazide within the same mechanism. Less paediatric use and a longer half-life.
verdict: alternative within the same mechanism, slightly weaker indication cover

mechanism_basis_note: appetite stimulation via H1 and 5-HT2 antagonism is well documented and is an indication-level match

key_counter_evidence: Malnutrition is a listed indication, so the grade rises to 2 from the previous pass. The previous pass also recorded a serotonin-antagonist mechanism; only the histamine H1 receptor antagonism is in the record. Weak evidence base in children, and sedation.

hypothesised_mechanism: pro-senescence induction in tumour cells, intended as the first step of an induce-then-clear sequence rather than as monotherapy
mechanism_is_registered: yes as a CDK4/6 inhibitor; the pro-senescence USE here is a hypothesis
mechanism_basis_note: CDK4/6 inhibition is registered; the pro-senescence CONSEQUENCE invoked here is documented downstream biology rather than the registered action
approval_source: openFDA /drug/ndc (product level) + Open Targets maximumClinicalStage (substance level)
key_counter_evidence: Added after the senescence axis was examined, because induction has approved chemistry while the clearance step does not have a paediatric-usable partner - so the sequence is currently half-available. Two objections, and the second is the same one that removed the tyrosine-kinase senolytic from this list: it acts on normal proliferating tissue, with neutropenia as the dose-limiting toxicity, and antiproliferative pressure is unwelcome in a child whose presenting complaint is growth failure. Induction without clearance leaves SASP-positive cells in a cancer-predisposition background.
verdict: tumour-arm hypothesis, coherent only as a sequence, and the second half of that sequence is missing

key_counter_evidence: Cachexia is a listed indication. Hormonal, with adrenal suppression risk, in a child who also has a cancer predisposition - hence the highest risk penalty in the symptomatic category.

mechanism_basis_note: selective vulnerability of aneuploid cells to metabolic stress is an inference from the aneuploidy literature rather than established metformin pharmacology - this is the weakest basis in the table and is one reason the risk penalty is 3
approval_source: openFDA /drug/ndc (product level) + Open Targets maximumClinicalStage (substance level)
product_level_verified: YES - FDA NDA + 16 ANDA + authorized generic
contraindication_flag: CAUTION - black box warning (lactic acidosis); antiproliferative pressure unwelcome in a child with growth failure
key_counter_evidence: Retained on request. Ceiling is low and the risk penalty is the highest in the table: black box warning against chronic paediatric exposure, plus antiproliferative pressure in a child whose presenting complaint is growth failure. The direction-of-effect tension is unresolved - metabolic stress argued to harm tumour cells also acts on somatic tissue.
